text.p: French freight forwarding firm Geodis has decided to suspend operations in Israel due to economic and political difficulties, officials said on Wednesday.

The company's Israeli subsidiary said in a letter to its clients dated April 23: "The Group Geodis in France, whereof Calberson (Israel) Ltd constitutes a part, has decided to cease temporarily the activities of its Israeli company".

"The decision has been reached by Group Geodis as conjuncture of the recent economic situation in Israel and the difficulties of political order in Israel in the fulfillment of peace treaties with its neighbour countries," said the letter, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.
"As soon as the situation enables it, Calberson (Israel) Ltd will reactivate its activities in the field of international freight forwarding," the letter, written in English, said.
Calberson (Israel) general manager Moshe Ben Adereth said he could not elaborate on the contents of the letter. He said the company's office in Israel would be closed.
Mandy Barak, in charge of ties with the Arab world at the Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce, said such a letter was unprecedented.
"It's surprising because usually when companies write commercial letters, political issues are not mentioned. This is the first time we are facing such a letter from a foreign company," he said.

Barak, who is also secretary of Israel's freight forwarding association, said freight forwarders are global companies with close ties between agents. "Freight forwarders usually work everywhere in the world," he said.
The Tel Aviv-based subsidiary has about 800 clients in Israel, Barak said.

Barak said he could not speculate on whether the company might be facing pressure from Arab countries to sever ties with Israel. But he noted that the parent company was having financial difficulties.
Geodis announced on April 23 that it planned to halt "non-strategic" activities in 1997 following losses last year.
Israel's groundbreaking of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem has plunged peacemaking with the Palestinians into crisis and soured relations with Arab countries.
Arab foreign ministers called a month ago for a suspension of normal dealings with Israel while "maintaining" and "reactivating" the primary Arab boycott.

Israel's economy, meanwhile, is slowing after five years of strong growth, and Finance Minister Dan Meridor told investors early this month the economy could expand less than four percent this year. He believed however, the slowdown was temporary.
